page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-256GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores using a shared allocation model, powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include GPU hardware. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng performance falls in the bottom 10%, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and moderate clock speed. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and PassMark CPU scores reach average levels. The server demonstrates strong multi-threaded capabilities, with bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU physics, and PassMark CPU encryption tests all placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations consistently register in the middle 50% tier.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU allocation, which limits sustained single-core execution speeds but offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-heavy workloads. This resource density makes the server appropriate for multi-threaded processing, memory-intensive database operations, caching layers, and moderate web serving workloads that benefit from a large memory footprint without requiring dedicated CPU cores or local storage.
